content: Do not hold on to someone who is leaving, for you will not meet the one who is arriving.
author: Carl Jung
story:
Rather than offering a polite platitude, this observation challenges how we navigate our inner lives. Thinking about doing something gives us a comfortable dopamine hit of progress without any of the actual friction. We often use over-researching and planning as socially acceptable disguises for fear of starting.

Carl Jung understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. Clarity follows action; it does not precede it. You cannot think your way into a new way of living—you have to act your way into a new way of understanding. The smallest real-world step beats the most brilliant theory.
reflectionPrompt: What would change in your daily outlook if you truly lived by this perspective?
